summary: The batch is clean on brands, gore and politics, and most fire objects already say 'grown-ups' (sparkler gloves, matchstick fire dropped in the sink, box-free candles). Several single lines are genuinely funny (birthday candles' smoke alarm singing, bonfire making the fireworks wait, elevator that will not stop at four, urinal with a mountain view, chess clock pyjama game, monocle dog, soda can 'bike, can, plane, can'). The structural problems are serious and batch-wide. (1) Legendaries: 26 of 101 are the 'has done X for N years / never once / still' formula, and most of the rest are wholesome but have no punchline (lost dog reunited, hikers rescued, a famous inventor's first experiment). (2) Epics: about 70 are 'every X at the Y at once' or 'the whole family/class/street' crowd scenes with no joke. (3) Rares: roughly 40 are the object doing its job well (fire screen catches sparks, plunger unblocks fast, tripod holds still, inhaler helps breathing, flare signals far). (4) Legendary names: 76 of 101 are 'The X That Y', plus four 'Professor/Doctor -worth of the Lab'. (5) Names sit on the wrong rarity in about 15 objects (glass door, toilet seat cover, thermometer, shutter, keyhole, garage door, door handle, rear-view mirror, compact mirror, crumpled paper, bin bag, sparkler, digital alarm, match). (6) The requested clusters are near-identical in places: two lantern-guides-hikers Legendaries plus the campfire rescue, two 'made it to the lorry/down the stairs without a rip' bin-bag Legendaries, toilet paper vs roll holder ('family of six, which nobody can explain'), car mirror vs rear-view mirror (lost dog following the car), band-aid vs first-aid box Epics (sports day, ran out), three lab 'famous scientist' Legendaries and three foam-overflow Epics, three dawn light stripes (blinds, curtain, shutter), landfill vs rubbish heap gulls. (7) Cross-batch near-copies: matchstick model village (w08 matchbox), incense Epic and Legendary (w11 incense stick), soda can Epic (w11 cigarette butt), tripod Epic (w11 easel), pillar candle Rare (w10 torch), binoculars stand (w06 parking meter, w10 binoculars). Safety: the firework Common jokes about waiting after lighting until people think it has gone out, which is the exact dangerous situation, and must change. The bonfire 'half raw sausages' line, the magnifier's focused hot spot and the firework that 'went off at the wrong end of the field' near a crowd should go. The matchstick village has a church tower (religion). The smartwatch Legendary (heart beating oddly) and the inhaler 'Medicine Taste' move are too medical for the tone. The odometer 'tiny slot machine' simile is a gambling reference. Toilets are mostly tasteful, except the urinal 'splashes back' Common. Moves are mostly truthful to the mechanics. The weak spots are clumsy suffixed names ('Reflection Guard Window', 'Gurgle Crack Seat', 'Wax Melt Snatch Snatch', 'Hair Check Boost Boost'), Ultimates that repeat the Epic name (cuckoo, grandfather clock, curtain, lab flask, matchstick), and variant Ultimates named after one effect ('Daze', 'Flash', 'Glare', 'Hail', 'Pong' where some variants burn or poison). Concrete replacements are given for every high and medium item. Names are checked for uniqueness against all curated files and the Pilot 01 proposal.

patterns.pattern: Legendary is the 'has done X for N years / never once / still has' formula: an endurance record, not an outrageous feat with a punchline.
patterns.suggestion: Rewrite each as one impossible achievement with a deflating, in-character punchline (see issues: blinds spelling HELLO in sunlight, sundial making the sun come out to check, cuckoo bird touring the forest, grandfather clock poking through the ceiling). Never 'for a hundred years' or 'still keeps perfect time'.

patterns.pattern: Legendary is sincere and heartwarming but has no joke (rescues, reunions, a famous scientist's first experiment, a town kept healthy).
patterns.suggestion: Keep the warmth if you like, but add a punchline that undercuts it (plunger: 'plus two socks, a toy car and the drain'; landfill: 'the sledgers still find the odd teapot').

patterns.pattern: Epic is a crowd scene ('every X at the Y at once', 'the whole family/class/street') with a comparison or no joke at all, instead of a concrete large-scale consequence.
patterns.suggestion: Make something physically happen with a specific funny result (cuckoo: a real cuckoo lays its egg in the little door; window: every school report blows across town; toilet seat cover: the visiting sheepdog herds them).

patterns.pattern: Rare is the object doing its job well (or a plain trait), not a troublesome power.
patterns.suggestion: Give each Rare a power that causes trouble (odometer rolls back when reversing so grandad drives home backwards; sundial moves its shadow so it is always half past ice cream; telescope spots next week's weather).

patterns.pattern: Legendary name monotony: 76 of 101 are 'The X That Y', and four science objects use 'Professor/Doctor X-sworth of the Lab'.
patterns.suggestion: Mix shapes: 'Name, the Epithet', a single coined name, a title + name, a compound. Per-id names are given where the lore changes; for the others pick from 'Name, the ...' or a single coined word (low issues are not listed individually for every untouched one).

patterns.pattern: Monster name describes another rarity's lore (or contradicts its own).
patterns.suggestion: Re-pair per the issues (glass door: C 'Walkintoer'; toilet seat cover: C 'Slideslipper', U 'Fluffycover'; thermometer: R 'Nosickday' and a new Legendary name).

patterns.pattern: Near-identical clusters inside the batch (the requested groups).
patterns.suggestion: Which side changes is named in each issue. Rules used: keep the stronger or earlier line, change the other; never let two objects in one cluster share a premise, a punchline shape or a Legendary name shape.

patterns.pattern: Near-copies of earlier drafts (w08, w10, w11, w06, w09, w05).
patterns.suggestion: Change the w12 side (replacements in the issues).

patterns.pattern: Fire objects: lines must keep grown-ups in charge and never model a risky behaviour.
patterns.suggestion: Firework Common must not joke about waiting near a lit firework; no half-raw sausages; no focusing sunlight into a hot spot; no misfire near a crowd. Replacements in the issues.

patterns.pattern: Clumsy suffixed or doubled move names.
patterns.suggestion: Drop the object word tacked on the end and doubled verbs ('Reflection Guard Window' -> 'Double Glazing', 'Hair Check Boost Boost' -> 'Last Look Boost').

patterns.pattern: Ultimate repeats the Epic monster name, or a variant Ultimate names only one effect.
patterns.suggestion: Give each finisher its own image and keep variant Ultimates effect-neutral (no Daze/Flash/Glare/Pong/Hail when other variants burn or poison).
